title: Variable Commitment Swap Matrix & Token Floor Simulation
body:
Executive summary:
This workbook simulates a small matrix of variable commitment swap options combined with an automated token price-floor trigger. Purpose: give finance, product, and sales a rapid decision surface for 1) converting short-term burst demand into staggered reserved commitments, 2) estimating headcount (FTE) impact under each conversion pattern, and 3) measuring unit economics (effective $/1k tokens) if we enforce a soft price-floor when capacity strain increases. This is intentionally compact — quick knobs for fast trade-off conversations.

Key assumptions (base):
- Baseline hosted blended cost per 1k tokens: $0.045 (includes infra, amortized GPU, networking).
- Average retail price per 1k tokens today: $0.12.
- Baseline monthly committed tokens (current customers): 350M tokens.
- Burst reserve pool (on-demand) average monthly: 150M tokens.
- Headcount mapping: 1 SRE = 10M sustained tokens/month throughput responsibility (ops/support + infra capacity management).
- Lead time to spin Dedicated capacity: 6–8 weeks (hiring or infra provisioning).
- Price-floor rule: if monthly tail latency breaches threshold AND burst utilization > 70%, trigger increment to effective price floor for new buys (not retroactive).

Scenario matrix (simplified table):
Columns: Scenario | Monthly commit (M tokens) | Burst reserve (M tokens) | Effective price /1k ($) | Headcount delta (FTE) | Monthly gross margin (%) | Notes
Rows:
- Baseline | 350 | 150 | 0.120 | +0 | 62% | Current state, no change
- Soft-swap | 400 | 100 | 0.115 | -1 | 60% | Convert 50M burst -> 50M commit via 3mo flexible reserving; slight price concession to sign-ups
- Hard-swap | 500 | 0 | 0.108 | -4 | 55% | Aggressive pushes into 12mo commitments; reduces ops load but revenue per token lower
- Floor-trigger | 350 | 150 | 0.14 (new buyers only) | +0 | 68% | Reactive floor applied to on-demand purchases when utilization >70%
- Mixed-tilt | 420 | 80 | 0.12 | -2 | 61% | Hybrid approach: short-term commits + small floor on bursts

Short-form calculations (examples):
- Effective price = list-price * (1 - average discount) + floor-impact 
  Example Soft-swap: 0.12 * (1 - 0.04) = 0.1152 ~ 0.115
- Monthly gross margin = (effective price - blended cost) / effective price
  Example Baseline: (0.12 - 0.045) / 0.12 = 0.625 -> 62%

Headcount translation notes:
- Ops/SRE: incremental headcount attributed to burst management and incident load. Moving 100M tokens from burst to commit reduces ops burden by ~2 SRE (rule of thumb here).
- Sales/Acct Mgmt: converting burst to commit requires 0.2 AE per $100k ARR in new contract-served accounts; model assumes 1 AE per $500k ARR allocated as cross-sell support when aggressively converting.
- Support/CS: minor change, assumed absorbed into existing team for <10% incremental workload.

Sensitivity tests included in sheet (instructions for reviewer):
1) Elasticity sweep: vary discount offered on commits from 0% to 18% and observe churn / conversion assumed rates (conversion curve: 0%->6%, 6%->18%).
2) Cost shock: +25% to blended infra cost to test margin breach points and HC cut triggers.
3) Burst event: 2x month spike (instantaneous) to test floor trigger and failover behavior; check SLA breach risk and estimated emergency capacity cost.

Representative stress-case output (from the simulated pivot):
- If infra cost +25% and we maintain Baseline volumes: margin falls to 42% -> immediate recommendation: enact temporary floor (expected to increase effective price to ~0.13) or accelerate convert-to-commit promotions.
- If 50M tokens/month move from burst->commit (Soft-swap): expected ops delta -1.2 FTE, monthly cash delta +$4.5k (from margin change) but AP/ACV smoothing needed.
- If we apply Price-floor to new buys during a sustained 3-month burst period: churn risk increases 0.4% among small accounts but yields immediate margin protection, estimated NPV positive if floor lasts >5 months.

Decision levers and runbook (compact):
- Trigger criteria: set utilization and latency thresholds for the automated floor (recommended initial values: burst-utilization >70% for 7 consecutive days AND p95 latency > target).
- Offer ladder: 3mo flexible commit (low discount), 12mo commit (higher discount), and burst-cap top-up (no discount, price-floor applies).
- Activation authority: finance + infra lead sign-off for >30 day floors; SRE lead can approve 72hr emergency floors.

Open questions / data gaps (for follow-up):
- Real conversion elasticity vs. discount for our mix of customers (we are using proxy curves from last year; need fresh A/B).
- Precise marginal infra cost per token at >80% utilization on our primary regions.
- ARPA distribution for accounts currently in burst pool (to model churn risk more precisely).

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Run a segmented A/B pilot for the 3mo flexible commit offer (Sales + Product) — owner: Priya Nair — ETA: 2026-10-15
- Instrument p95 latency + burst-utilization alert to wire into the pricing runbook (SRE + Infra) — owner: Owen Martinez — ETA: 2026-09-18
- Feed updated ARPA distro to finance model and rerun sensitivity with real customer cohort data — owner: Maya Chen — ETA: 2026-09-25
